representation_correction.error: S1-S6 were treated as directly composable nodes although they are macro-strategy motifs.

sampling_disclaimer.description: These are manually auditable writer-generated DAG samples, not samples from a trained graph model.

strategy_nodes.name: result_first_pareto_ledger
strategy_nodes.role: select and order one quality comparison, one latency tradeoff, and one boundary

activate_when: word budget is near the lower allowed bound
system-level quality and latency are the primary reader questions
one limitation is sufficient for claim calibration

combinations.selection_reason: A one-node graph tests the minimum strategy structure that still exposes the quality-efficiency tradeoff and retrieval boundary.
possible_failure: Readers may not recover why individual architectural changes matter.

activate_when: component-level diagnostic recovery is also required
deactivate_when: the aggregate result must appear in the opening

combinations.selection_reason: The boundary constrains all later positive evidence, while the staircase preserves local mechanism-test links.
possible_failure: The abstract can become a sequence of measurements.

strategy_nodes.name: operating_point_decision_split
strategy_nodes.role: assign SISO and MIMO decision roles

strategy_nodes.name: evaluation_mosaic_with_scope_gate
strategy_nodes.role: assign nonredundant functions to formal-state and retrieval evaluations

typed_edges.condition: configuration choice is the primary question

activate_when: the reader must choose between speed and quality operating points
deactivate_when: recurrence ablations are the primary contribution

combinations.selection_reason: The decision split gives the evaluation mosaic a concrete entry point and prevents latency, formal-state, and retrieval evidence from being treated as interchangeable.
possible_failure: Deployment framing may crowd out architectural novelty.

strategy_nodes.name: salience_anchor_then_selective_bindings
strategy_nodes.role: bind a small number of diagnostic anchors

typed_edges.condition: early aggregate salience and local validation are jointly required

activate_when: the aggregate comparison must be immediately recoverable
at least two component checks must survive compression

combinations.selection_reason: S1 allocates the headline evidence budget; S5 prevents the method from becoming an unsupported list by attaching selective diagnostics.
possible_failure: Mechanisms can look post hoc after a result-led opening.
The selected diagnostics may omit a reader's preferred component.

strategy_nodes.name: evaluation_mosaic_with_scope_gate
strategy_nodes.role: assign each evaluation a distinct claim function

typed_edges.condition: retrieval risk must constrain all positive claims

activate_when: the reader values evaluation interpretability over a single headline
both risk calibration and component attribution are required
deactivate_when: a compact deployment decision is the primary goal

combinations.selection_reason: The triple graph treats the abstract as a scoped diagnostic audit: boundary first, evaluation roles second, local bindings third.
possible_failure: The narrative may resemble an audit checklist.
The aggregate contribution may be underemphasized.

strategy_nodes.name: salience_anchor_then_selective_bindings
strategy_nodes.role: produce the common problem, method, and early quality anchor

control_nodes.role: merge activated branches without universalizing their claims

branches.both_binding: activate S6 and S4 in parallel

combinations.selection_reason: A common salient core is followed only by context-relevant branches; the example activates both to show a valid fork-and-join realization.
possible_failure: Activating both branches can erase conditional sparsity.
Branch joins may produce a generic conclusion.
Context gates are proposed, not learned or calibrated.
